title: Paper-default deep neural memory validation before Stage C genomic scaling
scientific_motivation: Establish that the paper-default two-layer associative memory follows its stated mathematics, remains numerically stable, resumes exactly, and develops non-trivial sequence-dependent state before committing A100 time to the 25M genomic study.

hypotheses.engineering: The exact paper recurrence and the preregistered RMS-stabilized recurrence remain finite for 500 optimizer steps at compact T4 scale and reproduce checkpoint/resume state.
hypotheses.behavioral: Adaptive deep memory improves held-out BPB or controlled delayed-association behavior over frozen-memory, no-memory, and shallow-memory controls at equal one-million-base budgets.
hypotheses.representation: Deep-memory state and retrieval traces contain reproducible variation beyond local GC composition and stream position.

scope_limitations: This protocol validates architecture, numerical behavior, and exploratory learning signal; it does not establish the final 25M memory-benefit claim.
Compact T4 results do not substitute for matched medium-model controls or second-seed replication.
The current stream manifest has no frozen ORF/intergenic labels, so functional region analyses are deferred.

claim_language.supported: paper-default deep memory is implemented faithfully and is sufficiently stable and behaviorally non-trivial to justify scaling
claim_language.not_supported: functional genomic interpretation, anomaly-detection utility, or superiority of adaptive memory at 25M scale

dataset.eligibility: unchanged E. coli plus Escherichia train-only selection from Stage C v1
dataset.balance: unchanged clade and GC balancing from Stage C v1
dataset.isolation: validation accessions remain excluded from fitting and compact model selection

tokenizer.name: frozen nonoverlap_6mer_v1 selected by Stage C v1
tokenizer.normalization: unchanged from the frozen Stage C stream manifest

paper_deep_memory.projections: causal depthwise Q/K/V convolution, kernel 4; L2-normalized Q and K
paper_deep_memory.gates: input-dependent alpha, eta, theta vectors per memory layer output channel
paper_deep_memory.backend: exact accelerated functional update with exact-reference parity

medium_25m_after_gate.status: ineligible until compact stability and behavior gates pass

decision_gates.mathematical: FP64 one-step recurrence, channel broadcasting, causal convolution history, and reference/accelerated parity tests all pass.
decision_gates.stability: All losses, fast weights, surprise states, projection histories, and gradients remain finite for 500 steps; checkpoint reload/resume verification passes.
decision_gates.policy_selection: Prefer paper_exact if its stability and resume gates pass; otherwise use stabilized_rms_v1 and report every conditioning intervention.
decision_gates.behavior: Proceed to medium adaptive discovery only if deep adaptive shows a favorable held-out BPB trajectory or delayed-association gain and its memory traces are non-degenerate.
decision_gates.stop: Do not scale if adaptive deep memory is non-finite, indistinguishable from controls within compact uncertainty, or represented only by stream position/GC baselines.

exploratory: retrieval, surprise, drift, gate, and conditioning trajectories
PCA of hidden and fast-memory state summaries
associations with GC, clade, accession, and stream position

prohibited_inferences: A compact behavior gain is not a final adaptive-memory benefit claim.
Memory-state separability is not evidence of biological function.
Generation plausibility is not promoter, gene, or fitness validation.
No 25M or anomaly-detection claim is permitted without the separate matched-control protocol.
